title: Personal Checking: Overdraft Protection Links to Savings and Transfer Fees
content:
## The link

Each Personal Checking account can have one savings account standing behind it as its source of overdraft protection. Recording such a link requires, from the bank's records:

- **Same owner** — one customer owns both the savings account and the checking account;
- **Active savings** — the savings account is active at the moment the link is recorded;
- **Eligible savings tier** — the savings account's tier is one that the Savings & Money Market Accounts terms mark as eligible to serve as an overdraft protection source.

Taking a link off is permitted at any time.

## The transfer

When a debit would push the checking ledger below zero and a link is in place, one transfer is made for that debit, sized to the shortfall — the exact sum that brings the checking ledger to zero once the debit is booked. The transfer appears on the checking account as an overdraft protection transfer entry naming the covered debit as its source, with a matching withdrawal on the savings side; whether that withdrawal uses up any savings withdrawal allowance is decided under the savings terms. A debit paid this way is not an overdraft and draws no overdraft item fee.

## Transfer fee

Each transfer draws the checking tier's overdraft protection transfer fee, booked as a fee entry that names the transfer as its source. An account is charged no more of these fees in one business day than its tier's daily ceiling. A tier whose transfer fee is 0.00 books nothing.

## Retired clause

As a statement of general reach, the older wording — a transfer only when the savings money on hand at that instant meets the entire shortfall, and never a partial one — is **no longer in force**. What replaced it keeps that whole-shortfall condition, with no partial transfers, for the transfers themselves; a Personal Checking fee refund decision that lays down its own test of whether a transfer would have paid an item uses that test instead.

## Hypothetical example

A linked, eligible savings account holds 300.00 USD. The checking ledger stands at 45.00 USD when a 120.00 USD debit posts. The shortfall is 75.00 USD, so one transfer of 75.00 USD moves in, the checking ledger lands at exactly zero, and the debit is not an overdraft. On a tier that prices transfers, one transfer fee follows, subject to the daily ceiling.

superseded_clauses: the transfer is made only if the savings current_balance at that moment covers the whole shortfall, and a partial transfer is never made.
